event_overview.title: About 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.subject: 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.summary: The September 11th Victim Compensation Fund (VCF) is a federally funded, no-fault compensation program for people who suffered eligible physical harm or died as a result of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks or related debris-removal work. It is distinct from the World Trade Center Health Program: the VCF provides financial compensation, while the health program provides monitoring and treatment for certified conditions.

facts.label: Origins and duration
facts.value: Congress created the original fund in 2001; it operated from 2001 to 2004. The James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act reactivated it in 2011, and the 2019 permanent-authorization law set an October 1, 2090 claim-filing deadline and provides funding necessary for approved claims.

facts.label: Purpose and legal scope
facts.value: The VCF compensates eligible individuals, or personal representatives of those who died, for physical injury, illness, or death connected to the September 11 attacks or immediate post-attack debris removal; it is designed as an alternative to tort litigation.

facts.label: Covered locations and periods
facts.value: For presence eligibility, the program recognizes the World Trade Center and surrounding New York City Exposure Zone from September 11, 2001 through May 30, 2002; the Pentagon site through November 19, 2001; and the Shanksville, Pennsylvania site through October 3, 2001.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The fund is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice, with a Special Master appointed by the Attorney General and operational support from DOJ's Civil Division.

facts.label: Relationship to health benefits
facts.value: VCF eligibility generally requires an eligible physical health condition and proof of presence; World Trade Center Health Program certification is accepted as proof of an eligible condition subject to other requirements. Enrollment in the health program does not automatically register someone with the VCF.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers anniversary-related advocacy and commemoration connected to 9/11 victims; it does not attempt to track every VCF claim, award, health-program development, or related lawsuit.

explore_lenses.title: Military pressure, civilian harm and diesel markets converged
explore_lenses.summary: Ukraine has treated Russian oil infrastructure as part of Moscow's war-funding and logistics base, while Russia's campaign against Ukraine's power and heating systems has produced severe civilian consequences. Trump's intervention focused on the separate global diesel-supply effects.

Trump urged Zelenskyy on September 13 to stop attacks on Russian diesel production and distribution, arguing they were worsening a global shortage.

story_report.summary: President Donald Trump said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to stop targeting each other’s energy facilities, after he criticized Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and urged Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian diesel infrastructure. The reported arrangement, if carried out, would narrow a campaign that has struck energy systems on both sides of the war, though its scope and enforcement have not been publicly defined.

sections.heading: Energy Strikes Affect Civilian Services
sections.body: Ukraine has carried out long-range attacks on Russia’s oil and gas industry for months, saying the sector finances and directly fuels Russia’s invasion. AP reported the strikes contributed to fuel rationing in Russia and a July ban on diesel exports, while the International Energy Agency said refining disruptions compounded reduced Gulf diesel and gasoil exports after the Iran war began. The UN has also documented repeated Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy and heating infrastructure that disrupted electricity, water, health care and schools.

sections.heading: Implementation Details Remain Unclear
sections.body: Large-scale exchanges continued the night before Trump’s announcement, according to AP: Ukraine said it struck a refinery and oil-storage facilities, while Russia used drones against Odesa and western Ukraine. Reporting identified no implementation date, verification body, diplomatic meeting or public process for deciding alleged violations. It also remains unclear whether refineries and fuel logistics fall within the definition of energy targets.

sections.heading: United Nations Seeks Wider Ceasefire
sections.body: The UN secretary-general has called for urgent de-escalation leading to a full, immediate and unconditional ceasefire, an objective broader than a halt on attacks against energy facilities. The UN said documented energy attacks appeared to violate core international-humanitarian-law principles, while noting that a facility’s military role and civilian effects must be assessed case by case.

facts.label: Purpose and legal scope
facts.value: The VCF compensates eligible individuals, or personal representatives of those who died, for physical injury, illness, or death connected to the September 11 attacks or immediate post-attack debris removal; it is designed as an alternative to tort litigation.

facts.label: Covered locations and periods
facts.value: For presence eligibility, the program recognizes the World Trade Center and surrounding New York City Exposure Zone from September 11, 2001 through May 30, 2002; the Pentagon site through November 19, 2001; and the Shanksville, Pennsylvania site through October 3, 2001.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The fund is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice, with a Special Master appointed by the Attorney General and operational support from DOJ's Civil Division.

facts.label: Relationship to health benefits
facts.value: VCF eligibility generally requires an eligible physical health condition and proof of presence; World Trade Center Health Program certification is accepted as proof of an eligible condition subject to other requirements. Enrollment in the health program does not automatically register someone with the VCF.

event_overview.title: About 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.subject: 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.summary: The September 11th Victim Compensation Fund (VCF) is a federally funded, no-fault compensation program for people who suffered eligible physical harm or died as a result of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks or related debris-removal work. It is distinct from the World Trade Center Health Program: the VCF provides financial compensation, while the health program provides monitoring and treatment for certified conditions.

facts.label: Origins and duration
facts.value: Congress created the original fund in 2001; it operated from 2001 to 2004. The James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act reactivated it in 2011, and the 2019 permanent-authorization law set an October 1, 2090 claim-filing deadline and provides funding necessary for approved claims.

facts.label: Purpose and legal scope
facts.value: The VCF compensates eligible individuals, or personal representatives of those who died, for physical injury, illness, or death connected to the September 11 attacks or immediate post-attack debris removal; it is designed as an alternative to tort litigation.

facts.label: Covered locations and periods
facts.value: For presence eligibility, the program recognizes the World Trade Center and surrounding New York City Exposure Zone from September 11, 2001 through May 30, 2002; the Pentagon site through November 19, 2001; and the Shanksville, Pennsylvania site through October 3, 2001.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The fund is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice, with a Special Master appointed by the Attorney General and operational support from DOJ's Civil Division.

facts.label: Relationship to health benefits
facts.value: VCF eligibility generally requires an eligible physical health condition and proof of presence; World Trade Center Health Program certification is accepted as proof of an eligible condition subject to other requirements. Enrollment in the health program does not automatically register someone with the VCF.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers anniversary-related advocacy and commemoration connected to 9/11 victims; it does not attempt to track every VCF claim, award, health-program development, or related lawsuit.

sections.heading: Bob Mackie’s Costume-Making Philosophy

His official biography lists nine Emmy wins, three Oscar nominations and a 2019 Tony Award for The Cher Show.

sections.heading: Bob Mackie’s Designs in Museums

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

story_report.summary: A Russian drone struck the locomotive of a Warsaw-bound passenger train in Ukraine’s Volyn region, about 2 km from the Polish border, shortly after a train carrying foreign dignitaries had passed through the area. Ukrainian Railways said no one was injured. PKP Intercity reported that 206 passengers were aboard; the train later reached Warsaw after a delay of about 370 minutes. Poland and Ukraine condemned the incident as an escalation, while EU foreign-policy chief Kaja Kallas said it was intended to intimidate Western supporters of Ukraine.

sections.heading: Border crossings and transport disruption
sections.body: A separate drone strike near the Dorohusk-Yahodyn crossing hit a truck less than 1 km from the Polish border, leading authorities to temporarily close the crossing before operations resumed. The disruption affected an area of strategic importance: Reuters reported that crossings on Ukraine’s border with Poland handle a significant share of allied military and humanitarian assistance entering Ukraine. The delayed Warsaw-bound train added to the immediate transport effects of the attack.

sections.heading: Russian and Ukrainian accounts of strike
sections.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia had deliberately hit the train’s locomotive, while Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha characterized strikes near Yahodyn as a direct threat at the EU and NATO frontier. Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces had targeted railway infrastructure used to transport military cargo from European countries. That statement is Moscow’s stated rationale and does not independently establish the target of this particular strike.

event_overview.title: About Gaza Conflict
event_overview.subject: Gaza Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Gaza conflict refers here to the war that began after Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups attacked Israel on October 7, 2023, killing people and taking hostages, followed by Israel's large-scale military campaign in the Gaza Strip. It involves Israeli forces, Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups, as well as Gaza's civilian population, and has produced major humanitarian, diplomatic and legal consequences.

facts.label: Start of current war
facts.value: The current phase began on October 7, 2023, when Hamas and other armed groups launched attacks from Gaza into Israel; Israel subsequently declared war and began Operation Iron Swords, including air, land and sea strikes in Gaza.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The principal battlefield is the Gaza Strip, a densely populated Palestinian territory on the Mediterranean coast bordering Israel and Egypt; the conflict's effects and related violence also extend to Israel, the West Bank and the wider region.

facts.label: Main parties
facts.value: The central belligerents are Israel and Hamas, alongside other Palestinian armed groups. The conflict also directly affects Palestinian civilians in Gaza and Israeli civilians, including people taken hostage during the October 7 attacks.

facts.label: Humanitarian dimension
facts.value: Hostilities have disrupted civilian services and humanitarian relief in Gaza; UN reporting has described obstacles to communications, medical response and aid delivery during the conflict.

facts.label: International legal proceedings
facts.value: South Africa instituted proceedings against Israel at the International Court of Justice on December 29, 2023, alleging violations of the Genocide Convention in Gaza. In January 2024, the Court indicated binding provisional measures; these were interim measures and did not decide the allegations on their merits.

event_overview.title: About 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.subject: 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.summary: The September 11th Victim Compensation Fund (VCF) is a federally funded, no-fault compensation program for people who suffered eligible physical harm or died as a result of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks or related debris-removal work. It is distinct from the World Trade Center Health Program: the VCF provides financial compensation, while the health program provides monitoring and treatment for certified conditions.

facts.label: Origins and duration
facts.value: Congress created the original fund in 2001; it operated from 2001 to 2004. The James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act reactivated it in 2011, and the 2019 permanent-authorization law set an October 1, 2090 claim-filing deadline and provides funding necessary for approved claims.

facts.label: Purpose and legal scope
facts.value: The VCF compensates eligible individuals, or personal representatives of those who died, for physical injury, illness, or death connected to the September 11 attacks or immediate post-attack debris removal; it is designed as an alternative to tort litigation.

facts.label: Covered locations and periods
facts.value: For presence eligibility, the program recognizes the World Trade Center and surrounding New York City Exposure Zone from September 11, 2001 through May 30, 2002; the Pentagon site through November 19, 2001; and the Shanksville, Pennsylvania site through October 3, 2001.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The fund is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice, with a Special Master appointed by the Attorney General and operational support from DOJ's Civil Division.

facts.label: Relationship to health benefits
facts.value: VCF eligibility generally requires an eligible physical health condition and proof of presence; World Trade Center Health Program certification is accepted as proof of an eligible condition subject to other requirements. Enrollment in the health program does not automatically register someone with the VCF.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers anniversary-related advocacy and commemoration connected to 9/11 victims; it does not attempt to track every VCF claim, award, health-program development, or related lawsuit.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

The findings detail the conditions faced by detainees at this facility, which has since been shuttered.
